result.summary: This PR changes HAVE_SYSTEM from `#cmakedefine` to `#cmakedefine01` in the CMake build config header so that the macro is always defined as 0 or 1 instead of left undefined, avoiding a -Wundef warning. The author noticed the warning while building the libbitcoinkernel library for iOS. The diff is a single line change.
result.problem: When HAVE_SYSTEM is unavailable, leaving the macro undefined triggers -Wundef warnings for anyone compiling with that flag, such as the author building the kernel library for iOS.

open_concerns: fanquake objects to making an isolated, seemingly arbitrary style change without broader justification
hebasto suggests simply reverting the original commit that introduced the #cmakedefine style instead of this fix
maflcko suggests standardizing on one style project-wide and enforcing it with a linter rather than a one-off change
resolved_concerns: Author dropped an unrelated HAVE_FDATASYNC change after fanquake's pushback, addressing part of the initial complaint

result.card: This PR makes HAVE_SYSTEM always defined as 0 or 1 via #cmakedefine01 instead of leaving it undefined, to silence a -Wundef warning the author hit while building libbitcoinkernel for iOS. It is a one-line change in cmake/bitcoin-build-config.h.in. Three maintainers (fanquake, hebasto, maflcko) pushed back with different alternative approaches (calling it an unjustified isolated change, suggesting a revert of the original commit, or suggesting a project-wide linter-enforced style) and the disagreement is unresolved. The problem it fixes is narrow, affecting only builds with -Wundef enabled in unusual configurations. No dependencies or blocking issues beyond the open approach dispute. Priority within build is low (P4) given its cosmetic, narrow scope.
